302.description: The handshake is over and the browser is sent on to the returnTo of the start, a path of this application. For the login intent, when the identity is linked to an account that can sign in, a new full session cookie is set; so it is for an identity nobody linked when the provider asserted its address as verified and either an enabled account that has verified that address gets the identity linked, or the provider allows accounts to be created, the address passes its allowed domains and the registration policy accepts it, and an account is created and the identity linked to it. For the invite intent, when the provider asserts the invited address, and no other, as verified, the identity is linked to the account it belongs to or to the enabled account that holds the invited address verified, or an account is created for the invited address (whatever the provider's auto-create setting says, because the invitation authorises it, and when the registration policy accepts it), the account becomes a member of the invitation's workspace with exactly the invited role, the invitation is accepted, and a new full session cookie is set that acts in that workspace. For the link intent the identity is added to the account that started the handshake, which must be the account of the browser's current session, and no session changes. For the reauth intent the browser's current session, which must be a session of the account that started the handshake and of an account the provider's identity is linked to, counts as re-authenticated from now. For every other outcome (a missing, reused, expired or foreign state, a refusal by the provider, a token that fails validation, an identity nobody linked whose address the provider did not assert as verified or that neither links nor creates an account, an invite intent whose provider address is not the invited one or is not verified or whose invitation is no longer pending, an address held by an unverified account, a disabled account, a registration the policy refuses, a link or reauth in a browser whose session is not the one that started it, a link whose session has not re-authenticated within the last ten minutes at the callback, an identity already linked to another account) nothing is changed and the browser goes to /login?error=oidc_failed, one answer that does not say which. The pre-auth cookie is cleared either way

Where the browser goes once the handshake is over: a path of this application, such as /go/docs. Anything else is ignored and the browser goes to /. The invite intent ignores it too and always ends on /

What the handshake is for. `login` (the default) signs in the account the identity is linked to. `link` adds the identity to the signed-in account and, because a linked identity outlives a password change and the end of every session, needs a session that re-authenticated within the last ten minutes: otherwise the start is answered `401 reauth_required` (re-authenticate with `POST /me/reauth` or the `reauth` intent, then start again), and the callback checks the same window. `reauth` proves the signed-in account's member at the provider, which counts as a re-authentication of the session for ten minutes. `link` and `reauth` need a complete session; all three of `link`, `reauth` and `invite` need the browser to report the request as coming from the application itself (Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin, or none for the address bar), and a request from another site or without that header is refused. `invite` accepts the invitation named by `invitation` through the provider, as the invited person; the session the acceptance makes replaces the one the browser carries. It counts against the token-redemption limits of the client address and, for a browser with a complete session, of its account
The token of the invitation link, from the path of /invite/<token>. Sent with the `invite` intent and with no other; the server keeps only its hash with the handshake
